name: Beans & Lentils
summary: Soaking or not, simmering times for dried beans and lentils, salting, and swapping in canned beans.

sections.heading: To soak or not
blocks: Soaking dried beans overnight in plenty of water shortens cooking and helps them cook evenly; drain and rinse before cooking. No time? A **quick soak**: cover with water, boil for 2 minutes, then let them stand covered off the heat for an hour. Unsoaked beans work too, they just take longer. Lentils and split peas never need soaking.

sections.heading: Cooking
blocks: Cover soaked beans with 2 inches (5 cm) of fresh water, add a pinch of salt and any aromatics (onion, garlic, bay leaf), bring to a boil, then simmer gently, partly covered, until creamy all the way through. Taste several beans: they don't all finish at once.

rows: Longer if old; great for hummus when very soft
Must boil hard for 10 minutes first (see below)
No soaking; fall apart into soups and dal

blocks.text: Raw and undercooked kidney beans contain a toxin that causes severe stomach upset. Boil them hard for at least 10 minutes before simmering, and never cook dried kidney beans from raw in a slow cooker: it doesn't get hot enough.
Salt doesn't make beans tough, but acid (tomatoes, vinegar) and very hard water slow softening. Add acidic ingredients once the beans are tender.

sections.heading: Canned beans
blocks: One 15-ounce (425 g) can holds about 1 ½ cups of drained beans, about the same as ½ cup (90–100 g) of dried beans after cooking. Rinse canned beans to remove extra salt and the starchy liquid, unless a recipe uses it (chickpea liquid, aquafaba, whips like egg whites).
